title: Calibrated Hire Pipeline — Shadow-week Rotation (working draft)
content:
Context and intent:
This doc proposes a calibrated hiring pipeline addition: a paid, structured "shadow-week" for late-stage candidates (post-tech screens) to observe, collaborate and be evaluated across 3–4 cross-functional touchpoints. Purpose is twofold: improve signal on collaboration & product fit, and reduce early onboarding churn by previewing the actual day-to-day.

Scope:
- Applies to mid+ ICs across engineering, infra, platform, SRE and product-adjacent roles where cross-team interaction matters.
- Optional for entry-level / strictly IC roles unless hiring manager opts in.

Goals / success metrics (initial hypotheses):
- Increase new-hire retention at 90 days by 15% for cohorts that pass shadow-week vs historical baseline.
- Reduce post-offer withdrawals by improving candidate certainty (target -10%).
- Improve calibration of hiring panel ratings: introduce shadow-week rubric to reduce discordance between interviewers (target mean pairwise disagreement drop).

High-level pipeline (recommended):
1) Sourcing -> 2) Recruiter screen -> 3) Hiring manager screen -> 4) Technical interview loop -> 5) Take-home / microproject (when applicable) -> 6) Shadow-week (paid, 3–5 days) -> 7) Hiring committee sync + decision -> 8) Offer -> 9) Onboarding (30/60/90 with mentor plan)

Shadow-week design (3-workday core example) — each day ~4 hours scheduled + 1 hour evaluator debrief:
- Day 0 (pre-shadow admin): NDA (if required), read-only access provision, schedule & context email, mentor intro.
- Day 1: Eng pairing & code walkthrough — pairing on small fix, observe team standup, 60m paired session with assigned buddy.
- Day 2: Product & customer context — product triage tabletop, stakeholder pairing (PM/solutions), review recent customer bug/feature.
- Day 3: Systems & ops — join on-call rotation shadow or infra runbook review, small ops task (sandboxed), feedback session with hiring manager.

Evaluation rubric (flat structure for easy scoring):
- Role-signal (35%) — demonstrated domain fundamentals and problem-solving relevant to role (1–5).
- Collaboration & pairing (25%) — ability to work with others, ask clarifying Qs, iteration speed (1–5).
- Learning velocity & curiosity (15%) — picks up unfamiliar context, asks good follow-ups (1–5).
- Communication & customer-awareness (15%) — articulates tradeoffs, asks user-focused Qs (1–5).
- Risk & security hygiene (10%) — follows data/access rules, safe handling of artifacts (1–5).

Scoring: numeric 1–5; weighted total yields pass / borderline / no-pass bins (suggested cutoffs: pass >= 3.8, borderline 3.2–3.79, no-pass < 3.2). Each evaluator fills a short free-text prompt: "Great signal", "Ambiguous signal — concerns", "Culture fit notes", and an action recommendation (hire / hold / no-hire).

Interviewer / evaluator playbook (short checklist):
- Before shadow: read candidate resume + prior interview notes; confirm schedule & objectives; set up read-only accounts and ephemeral credentials; prep 1 microtask per day.
- During: take timestamped notes on examples of collaboration, ask one cross-functional question, avoid giving production credentials or PII.
- After: submit rubric within 48 hours; provide 3 bullet strengths / 3 bullet risk points.

Candidate logistics & experience (candidate-friendly):
- Paid at market hourly rate for shadow days (explicit in offer stage if scheduled pre-offer).
- Clear agenda, points of contact, expected outcomes.
- Option to decline shadow-week; declining does not automatically disqualify but does change signal set.

Onboarding tie-in (30-day slate recommended post-offer):
- Day 0: equipment, identity access, welcome doc + 1:1 with manager + buddy pairing.
- Week 1 checklist: meet core collaborators, setup dev environment, complete 1 small shipped change with buddy.
- Weeks 2–4: incremental ownership tasks, first-week retro with manager, measurable 30-day goals (deliverable + learning objectives).
- Mentor rotation: first 6 weeks weekly 30m sync; then biweekly through day 90.

Operational considerations & guardrails:
- Security: read-only clones and sandbox environments; no access to production secrets; IR checklist if candidate touches sensitive data.
- Legal & compensation: consult legal for NDAs and local labor rules (paid interviews vs contractor status).
- Scheduling: coordinate panel capacity; try to compress to contiguous days to reduce context switching.
- Data retention: evaluator notes live in hiring repository for 1 year, then archived.

Open questions / TODOs (working list):
- Compensation model: flat stipend vs hourly? (People Ops to propose by 2025-02-20).
- Which roles require mandatory shadow-week vs opt-in? propose default list and exceptions.
- Mechanism for candidates who are remote across time zones — compressed schedule or asynchronous microtasks?
- Standardized microtask bank: who owns and curates per team? (suggest product+eng pairing)

Quick reference templates (copyable):
- Candidate invite email: short agenda + attachments + access FAQ + contact info.
- Evaluator rubric form: 5 numeric items + 3 short text fields + recommendation dropdown.
- Onboarding 30-day goal template for hiring manager.

References & related artifacts:
- Confluence: Calibrated Hiring Playbook (linked above)
- Jira: RECRUIT-422 (pilot logistics)
- GitHub: talent-scripts/pull/18 (scheduling automation prototype)

Notes: this is an early draft — intended to be operationalized with a 6-week pilot across platform-engineering and infra teams. Primary owner for pilot: Avery Chen; pilot coordinator: Morgan Patel. Please add comments inline in Drive and tag people-ops.
summary: Working draft: introduce a paid, structured 3-day shadow-week for late-stage candidates to improve hiring signal and onboarding fit. Includes pipeline placement, detailed schedule, weighted rubric, onboarding tie-ins, and operational guardrails. Pilot recommended for mid+ technical hires.
